assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing turned genome editing from double-strand cutting into precise, programmable chemistry on a nucleobase, which is a chemist's contribution through evolved deaminase enzymes. It is a game-changer with real consequences: therapeutic base editors have reached patients. Simple concept, quantitative experimental validation.
assessment.attribution: Liu conceived and led the work, and Komor and Gaudelli made the first cytosine and adenine base editors as trainees. With a three-person limit and CRISPR already honored in 2020, a one-person or Liu-led configuration is cleanest. Kondo and Nishida (deaminase-nickase Target-AID) are independent but secondary.
assessment.maturity: About ten years since the first paper, independently reproduced and in clinical use. Timing appears right; the key concept is established and unlikely to be revised.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as an incremental extension of the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Long-term clinical safety and efficacy data are still accumulating.
Whether prime editing (B007) should be recognized together with or instead of base editing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ab initio molecular dynamics let bond breaking and forming, solvation and condensed-phase chemistry be simulated without empirical force fields. It is a foundational method used in thousands of studies, with quantitative links to experiment, and fits the committee's earlier recognition of computational chemistry.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 Car-Parrinello paper has two clear authors and a clean two-person prize. Parrinello's wider body of work (metadynamics, ML potentials) strengthens his case but should not crowd out Car.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use and validation; very mature, arguably late. Some may say density functional theory (1998) already covers the theme.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 1998 DFT recognition and Parrinello's other candidacies (B002, B015).
Relative weight versus more recent methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation opened a genuinely new pharmacological modality: event-driven catalytic destruction of proteins formerly considered undruggable. It is a game-changer, with degraders in late clinical trials. The molecular mechanism, from cereblon as the thalidomide target to ternary complex structure and cooperativity, is now well understood.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty. Crews and Deshaies delivered the PROTAC concept (with Sakamoto, Kim), Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target underlying molecular glues, and Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary complex structures were decisive for the field. Eight credited names exceed the limit, and the choice is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Clinical proof is arriving (e.g. late-stage degraders) but no approval of a PROTAC yet as far as I know. Strong science, slightly early.
uncertainties: No clear approved PROTAC drug; I may be mistaken about recent regulatory events.
Proper division of credit between PROTACs and molecular glues, and between Crews, Deshaies, Handa and Ciulli.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Expanding the genetic code with orthogonal tRNA-synthetase pairs allows site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids in living cells and organisms. This is original, simple in concept and now a routine tool for protein engineering, biophysics and therapeutics (ADCs, new-to-nature biochemistry).
assessment.attribution: Schultz and colleagues established the first in vivo incorporation; Wang as Schultz's co-worker, and Chin's later work on quadruplet codons, multi-site recoding and synthetic genomes. Yokoyama and Mehl are also plausible. A Schultz, Chin and Wang trio is reasonable but there is a priority question between Schultz's lab members.
assessment.maturity: Over 20 years of use, widely validated. Mature and, if anything, long overdue.
uncertainties: Chemical biology candidates are crowded; fitting the genetic code expansion into a three-person limit with Yokoyama and Mehl is uncertain.
Which Schultz lab member is the decisive co-discoverer.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C mutant cysteine with tethering-derived compounds broke the 'undruggable' dogma and led directly to approved drugs (sotorasib, adesagrasib). Chemical genetics of analog-sensitive kinases is an earlier, independent contribution. It is a clear game-changer with an immediate consequence.
assessment.attribution: Credited as a single person, which is clean for a prize with one or a few laureates. Contributions of industry teams on the clinical compounds are not included, and a fair prize might involve the covalent-ligand tethering methodology developers, which the supplied credit does not list.
assessment.maturity: KRAS G12C inhibitors are approved with several years of clinical experience, while resistance remains an issue. Reasonably mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee thinks the discovery is better described as drug discovery than basic chemistry.
Single-name attribution may omit relevant collaborators (my knowledge here is uncertain).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned potentials give near quantum-mechanical accuracy at force-field cost, which changes what can be simulated in chemistry and biomolecular modeling. This is my own field and I know the quality; the Behler-Parrinello neural network potential and Gaussian approximation potentials are the two decisive lines. They demonstrably reproduce experiment.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello (2007) introduced high-dimensional neural network potentials, Bartók and Csányi the GAP/SOAP approach. Behler, Parrinello and Csányi is a defensible trio, but Bartók and von Lilienfeld also contributed and the field is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Still maturing; transferability, long-range physics and training data issues are not fully resolved. Possibly premature relative to Car-Parrinello.
uncertainties: Premature relative to foundation models for materials and AlphaFold's 2024 recognition.
Overlap of Parrinello with B014 and B002.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing changed biology and medicine by reducing the cost of reading DNA by orders of magnitude. Solexa's reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis is clearly chemistry and has demonstrated enormous consequences.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented Solexa chemistry, while Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing platform was the first commercial NGS system. Mayer and Ju are other candidates. Credit is contested, and a fair three-person configuration is plausible but not certain.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with two decades of unambiguous impact. Possibly the most deserving of broad recognition but credit complexity remains.
uncertainties: Dispute over priority between competing platforms and chemistries.
The 1980 Sanger prize may be thought of as covering part of the territory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA and RNA molecules through protein nanopores moved from a concept to commercial long-read sequencing. A creative, simple idea (current blockade by a threaded polymer) with major consequences for genomics and molecular detection.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton proposed the strand-through-pore idea, Kasianowicz showed the first alpha-hemolysin results, Bayley engineered pores, and Akeson demonstrated enzyme-controlled ratcheting. This is a hard attribution case; Branton may no longer be living, which I have not verified.
assessment.maturity: Mature in practice, with robust independent commercial deployment, though accuracy still lags short-read methods in some areas.
uncertainties: Complex attribution across five credited names and the three-laureate limit.
Possible overlap with B028 as a sequencing prize.
Status of Branton is uncertain to me.
